basis: Benign smooth muscle tumour arising within a bronchus.
Microcephaly and intellectual disability define neurologic involvement; micromelia defines skeletal involvement.
Hereditary methemoglobinemia; impaired androgen synthesis with low DHEAS and elevated LH in 1/1 annotated patients supports endocrine involvement.
Autoimmune disease directly affecting intestinal mucosa and causing enteropathy.
Chronic bronchial inflammation and airflow obstruction; inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Intellectual disability defines the syndrome; renal dysplasia, anophthalmia and finger contractures each occur in 30-79%. Listed cardiac defects occur in 5-29%.
Corneal endothelial dystrophy causes corneal edema, opacity and visual impairment.
Carcinoma in situ originates in the hypopharynx; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Joubert brain malformation; coloboma affects 6/11 patients, supporting ocular involvement. Renal cysts/nephronophthisis affect at most 3/11 (<30%).
Inherited retinal disease; the neurologic ancestry does not establish disease outside the eye.
Acquired loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue defines this metabolic disorder. Associated diabetes and fatty liver are separate diseases.
Cerebellar ataxia, epilepsy and intellectual disability define the disorder; abnormal eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Infantile epileptic encephalopathy with developmental stagnation or regression. Nonspecific skin annotations do not establish direct damage from this syndrome.
Immune-mediated arthritis and enthesitis define the disease. Uveitis occurs in 5-29%; cardiac and renal involvement are rarer.
Tuberculous infection of the gastrointestinal tract, predominantly ileum and cecum; hepatic tuberculosis is a subtype rather than universal involvement.
B-cell developmental arrest causes absent circulating B cells and agammaglobulinemia. Otitis and pneumonia are separately diagnosed infections.
Disseminated tuberculosis with pulmonary micronodules; hepatic granulomatous involvement occurs in roughly 50-80%. CNS disease is a minority manifestation.
Immunodeficiency defines ICF4; intellectual disability affects 3/4 patients and motor delay 4/6, supporting common neurodevelopmental involvement.
Thiamine deficiency causes metabolic brain injury and persistent amnesia. Ocular motor abnormalities arise from neurologic dysfunction.
Severe developmental impairment, seizures and spasticity define the disorder; structural joint contractures occur in 2/6 patients (~33%), near the threshold.
Progressive chorioretinal and macular atrophy directly impair vision.
Congenital narrowing of the pulmonary heart valve; pulmonary here denotes the valve rather than lung disease.
Substance dependence is a psychiatric disorder; organ damage from particular substances is not inherent to this umbrella concept.
Fetal arterial duct constriction causes right ventricular pressure overload and valvular dysfunction. Respiratory distress alone does not establish lung damage.
Gonadal hormone failure and sensorimotor neuropathy define the syndrome; skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%. Gonadoblastoma occurs in only 5-29%.
